papers.title_en: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
papers.authors: Ziyong Wang, Yupei Lin, Runxuan Huang, Liang Lin, Dongyu Zhang, Guangrun Wang
papers.evidence: 用于接触丰富操作的触觉理解策略
papers.tldr: 接触丰富操作要求机器人理解触觉物理并动态调整动作，但现有学习策略依赖专门预训练和逐任务优化，成本高昂。本文提出GPT-as-Tactile-Policy，将专家演示总结为任务指导与触觉参考，由GPT-6-Astra结合多模态观察和交互历史生成控制命令并依据接触反馈调整。在五个UniVTAC任务上平均成功率达93.8%，插入孔任务从31%提升至99%，无需机器人特定微调即可与最先进策略相当，证明了通用多模态模型的物理理解与动作引导能力。
papers.abstract_en: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action. GPT-6-Astra combines this context with multimodal observations and interaction history to generate control commands and adjust actions through contact feedback. Without additional robotics-specific pretraining or per-task policy fine-tuning, our method achieves 93.8\% mean success across five UniVTAC tasks. Overall performance is comparable to state-of-the-art policies, with higher success on selected tasks. On Insert Hole, tactile feedback improves success from 31\% to 99\%. Execution analysis further demonstrates contact-guided probing and correction, supporting manipulation progress through explicit expert experience and online feedback.

papers.title_en: Tactile-Based Robotic Manipulation: From Mechanics-Driven to Data-Driven Perspectives
papers.authors: Jingyi Xiang, Yixuan Wang, Wenzhen Yuan
papers.evidence: 综述触觉驱动的机器人操作从力学驱动到数据驱动的方法
papers.tldr: 触觉传感为机器人提供接触界面物理交互的直接访问，是鲁棒灵巧操作的关键模态。研究范式从基于接触力学与任务推理的力学驱动，演进为直接从数据学习触觉表示与策略的数据驱动。本文系统回顾两种视角：力学驱动关注触觉信号形成状态表示并影响动作，数据驱动涵盖模仿学习、强化学习、VLA模型和预测模型。最后讨论可扩展、可泛化、鲁棒系统的开放挑战与未来机遇。
papers.abstract_en: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This paper reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing, and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision-language-action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.

papers.title_en: Embodied Task Agents Can Perform Fine Manipulation through Tactile In-Context Learning
papers.authors: Yubang Wang, Zezheng Huai, Yifei Zhang, Jinhao Wu, Yitong Chen, Haozhe Zhang, Sixian Li, Jingjing Gong, Zhenyang Lin, Ziyang Chen, Xipeng Qiu
papers.evidence: 触觉上下文学习实现无需任务特定训练的精细操作
papers.tldr: 现有 embodied task agents 依赖视觉难以完成精细操作，且缺乏无需训练即可利用触觉经验的方式。Tactile-ETA 通过上下文学习将触觉观察与视觉、本体感觉结合，从专家演示中提取关键触觉帧进行动作选择。在四个模拟任务中加入触觉观察使成功率从15.75%升至24.00%，真实机器人任务从0%升至60%。这证明触觉上下文学习用于精细操作的可行性，并指向多感官 agent 扩展路径。
papers.abstract_en: Can embodied task agents use tactile experience to perform fine manipulation without task-specific model training? We investigate this capability through Tactile-ETA, a system that incorporates tactile experience into an embodied task agent through in-context learning. Successful expert demonstrations show how contact changes during manipulation. We pair each recorded robot movement with its camera views and bilateral tactile observations. We keep tactile observations at the start and end of each movement and add two neighboring time points when the tactile images change markedly in between. The agent combines these demonstrations with current vision, tactile observations, and proprioception to select actions through general-purpose robot tools, without updating model parameters. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, adding tactile observations to the same two expert demonstrations increases average success from 15.75% to 24.00%, with current sensing and execution interfaces held fixed. Further experiments show that performance depends on the sensory content and representation of demonstrations, while comparing agent models on Lift Bottle reveals substantial differences under the same system configuration. On the real-robot tasks, demonstrations with aligned visual and tactile observations increase the task success rate from 0% to 60%. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using tactile experience in context for fine manipulation and suggest a path toward extending embodied task agents to additional sensory inputs.

papers.title_en: Learning Tactile-Aware Hand Representations from Human Hand-Object Interaction Data
papers.authors: Yeonguk Yu, Jaehong Kim, Byungok Han
papers.evidence: 利用人手物交互数据为灵巧操作学习触觉表征
papers.tldr: 机器人触觉表示学习通常依赖大量机器人数据收集，难以跨不同手和传感器扩展。HuTact 框架从大规模人-物交互数据预训练触觉感知手表示，无需真实触觉信号，并将人类手部运动中的交互结构迁移到机器人触觉观测。在抓取预测、滑动检测、物体分类等任务上，仅用 25% 标签数据加未标记机器人数据，抓取预测 Macro-F1 达 88.26%，与全量数据从头训练相当。这表明人类交互数据可作为机器人触觉学习可扩展的补充先验来源。
papers.abstract_en: Tactile representation learning for dexterous manipulation often requires substantial robot-side data collection, limiting its scalability across different hands and sensors. We explore whether large-scale human hand-object interaction (HOI) data can provide a useful prior for robotic tactile learning. To this end, we propose HuTact, a framework that pretrains tactile-aware hand representations from human HOI data without requiring real tactile signals during pretraining. HuTact transfers the interaction structure learned from human hand motions to robotic tactile observations and can be further adapted with a small amount of unlabeled robot interaction data. We evaluate HuTact on tactile perception and manipulation tasks, including grasp prediction, slip detection, object classification, and tactile-conditioned policy learning. Across these tasks, human HOI pretraining improves data efficiency and provides a strong initialization for downstream learning. Notably, with HOI pretraining followed by midtraining on unlabeled robot play data, HuTact achieves 88.26% Macro-F1 on grasp prediction using only 25\% of the labeled downstream data, comparable to training from scratch on the full labeled dataset (88.23%). These results suggest that human interaction data can serve as a scalable complementary source for robotic tactile representation learning.

papers.title_en: Large Multimodal Models for Direct Robot Control: GPT-6 as a Beginning
papers.authors: Youwei Zhou, Bohan Hou, Yankai Fu, Yaoxu Lyu, Yifan Ye, Shilin Shan, Chen Guo, Jiaming Liu, Ran He, Caifeng Shan, Shanghang Zhang, Jianfei Yang, Zhihe Lu
papers.evidence: 评估大模型用于机器人控制，展示触觉反馈修正动作
papers.tldr: 通用多模态模型的具身机器人控制能力仍不明确。本文系统评估GPT-6 Astra在闭环机器人操纵中的深度感知、具身上下文学习和触觉理解能力，并在五个基准上测试。结果显示模型在RoboDojo和RoboTwin 2.0上分别取得26.92%和76.0%成功率，但语义推理与物理执行之间存在明显差距，几何约束任务零样本成功仅11.1%。研究刻画了通用多模态模型的具身能力边界，并指出安全高效控制的关键挑战。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in visuospatial understanding and agentic reasoning enable direct robotic manipulation with general-purpose multimodal models, but their embodied capabilities remain poorly understood. This paper systematically evaluate GPT-6 Astra for closed-loop robotic manipulation using a lightweight agent execution framework. We first probe three fundamental embodied capabilities-depth perception, embodied in-context learning, and tactile understanding-and demonstrate that the model can exploit depth information, acquire simple manipulation strategies from contextual demonstrations, and use tactile feedback to correct its actions. We then evaluate GPT-6 Astra across five established manipulation benchmarks along six capability dimensions. Despite competitive performance on several benchmarks-26.92\% success on RoboDojo and 76.0\% on RoboTwin 2.0-our analysis reveals a pronounced gap between semantic reasoning and physical execution, particularly in consequence-aware action planning, precision, and complex motion coordination. To further examine these limitations, we introduce LIBERO-GeoMotion, a new benchmark of geometry-constrained tasks that require precise pose alignment, coordinated translation and rotation, and anticipation of physical action consequences. GPT-6 Astra achieves only 11.1\% zero-shot success, exposing the difficulty of translating spatial understanding into physically feasible motion. Real-world experiments corroborate these findings: zero-shot execution is feasible for simple tasks, yet persistent deficits remain in motion feasibility, precise control, and physical safety, while substantial inference latency further hinders practical deployment. Overall, our results characterize the emerging embodied capabilities of general-purpose multimodal models and delineate the key challenges toward safe, efficient, and reliable robotic manipulation.

papers.title_en: Touch-JEPA: Tactile Representation Learning from Hand-Object Video with Limited Tactile Supervision
papers.authors: Minseong Kweon, Qiao Feng, Yiming Huang, Lingjie Liu
papers.evidence: 从手-物视频中学习触觉表征，仅需有限触觉监督，面向物理智能系统
papers.tldr: 理解手-物交互中的接触和触觉强度是物理智能的关键，但受限于触觉测量的高成本与有限覆盖。Touch-JEPA利用手-物视频自监督预测手部表面掩码视觉特征，并可结合有限触觉监督联合学习。仅自监督预训练即可在接触判别和强度估计上超越监督基线，且迁移到机器人手无需触觉训练数据；联合学习与有限触觉监督进一步改善估计。这表明手-物视频可扩展自监督触觉表征学习，有限触觉测量提供物理接地。
papers.abstract_en: Understanding contact and tactile magnitude in hand-object interaction is a key step toward physically intelligent systems, yet learning such representations is limited by the cost and restricted coverage of tactile measurements. We present Touch-JEPA, a framework for learning tactile representations from hand-object videos with limited tactile supervision. We first introduce a self-supervised pretraining objective that learns from video alone without tactile supervision. Using video-derived hand geometry, Touch-JEPA predicts masked visual features at corresponding hand-surface locations from spatial and temporal context, encouraging the representation to capture latent contact dynamics. We then extend this formulation to joint representation learning, where masked prediction is applied to all videos while tactile supervision is available only for a labeled subset, grounding the shared representation in measured contact and magnitude. With self-supervised pretraining alone, simple supervised readouts on frozen Touch-JEPA features outperform supervised baselines in contact discrimination and tactile magnitude estimation across three human-hand benchmarks, and transfer to robotic hands without robot tactile training data. Joint learning with limited tactile supervision further improves contact and magnitude estimation on the human-hand benchmarks. Together, these results show that hand-object video can provide scalable self-supervision for tactile representation learning, while limited tactile measurements provide complementary physical grounding.

papers.title_en: Physical Canvas: A Vision Tactile World Model For Robot Policy Evaluation And Learning
papers.authors: Zebin Xing, Yuhang Zheng, Yupeng Zheng, Yichen Zhang, Zichen Li, Shangqing Zhou, Yujie Zang, Yuchen Liu, Zhongpu Xia, Haoran Li, Qichao Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向接触丰富操作的视觉触觉世界模型
papers.tldr: 机器人策略物理评估成本高且视觉世界模型常误导接触动力学，难以可靠反馈。PhysCanvas 是一个状态一致的视觉-触觉世界模型，统一多视角 RGB、触觉图像、标记位移和任务状态，通过运动图像对齐动作条件，并用三种奖励模型做一致性感知后训练。在四项真实操作任务中，世界模型与真实成功率的相关性从0.602提升至0.885，策略后训练成功率从59.1%提升至70.8%。这证明统一多模态建模和一致性后训练对机器人策略评估与学习具有重要价值。
papers.abstract_en: Evaluating and post-training robot policies through physical interaction is costly and difficult to scale, motivating action-conditioned world models as interactive simulators. However, visually plausible predictions can misrepresent contact dynamics, providing unreliable feedback for policy evaluation and learning. We introduce PhysCanvas, a state-consistent visuo-tactile world model for contact-rich robot manipulation. PhysCanvas unifies multi-view RGB, tactile images, marker displacement, task state, and actions within a unified vision space. All modalities share a video VAE and pretrained generative backbone, allowing optical touch to reuse visual and temporal priors. Motion images derived through forward kinematics and camera projection provide spatially aligned action conditioning, while an initial RGB anchor and updated reference observations guide sequential generation. Our consistency-aware post-training uses the frozen Scene Reward Model, Modality Reward Model, and State Reward Model to supervise scene preservation, visual-tactile compatibility, and agreement with real task outcomes. The resulting world model supports closed-loop policy rollouts for evaluation and provides imagined interactions and rewards for GRPO policy updates. Across four real-world manipulation tasks, when policies are rolled out in the world model, State Reward Model supervision increases the arithmetic mean of task-wise Pearson correlations between world-model and real-world success rates from 0.602 to 0.885. Policy post-training in the reward-guided world model further increases $π_{0.5}$'s mean real-world success rate from a 59.1% SFT baseline to 70.8%. These results demonstrate the value of unified multimodal modeling and consistency-aware post-training for robot policy evaluation and learning. Project page: https://zebinx.github.io/PhysCanvas_HomePage/.

papers.title_en: T-WLA: Bridging Slow Vision and Fast Touch
papers.authors: Kaichen Zhou, Yuzhen Chen, Hannah Yao, Chonghe Jiang, Rao Fu, Xihang Yu, Wei Dai, Bashar Kabbarah, Haoyu Chen, Ishita Goluguri, Zhiyang Dou, Haonan Chen, Fangneng Zhan, Mengyu Wang, Wojciech Matusik, Antonio Torralba, Paul Pu Liang
papers.evidence: 接触丰富操作中触觉修正动作
papers.tldr: 接触丰富操作中，视觉策略更新滞后导致接触条件变化时动作修正不及时。T-WLA采用共享视觉记忆架构，视觉分支生成基础动作，轻量触觉编辑器利用缓存记忆和触觉输入预测残差修正，无需重跑视觉分支。在EgoTouch和Tachin上，手指关节MPJPE相对最强基线降低30%；四个真实灵巧操作任务平均成功率达约50%。该架构有效桥接慢速视觉与快速触觉，提升接触丰富操作性能。
papers.abstract_en: In contact-rich manipulation, contact conditions can change before a visual policy updates its action plan. Recomputing the plan through the visual policy adds latency, while tactile feedback alone does not specify how the ongoing motion should be revised for the task. We introduce T-WLA, a world-language-action architecture that uses shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction. At each visual update, the visual branch integrates the current image, task instruction, and retrieved history into a visual memory that conditions base-action generation. The same memory is cached for a lightweight tactile editor, which combines it with the active action chunk and incoming touch to predict residual corrections to unexecuted actions without rerunning the visual branch. Future-image and future-pressure prediction provide training-only supervision, encouraging the visual memory and tactile features to capture interaction dynamics relevant to action generation and correction. We evaluate T-WLA on tactile-conditioned hand-motion prediction using EgoTouch and Tachin, and on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks. T-WLA reduces finger-joint MPJPE by 30% relative to the strongest reported baseline and achieves an average success rate of approximately 50.0% across real-robot manipulation tasks. Videos and code are available at https://anonymous-submission-20.github.io/T-WLA.github.io/.

papers.title_en: VecTile: A Low-Cost Flexible Tactile Array for 3-DoF Force Sensing
papers.authors: Jian Hou, Xin Zhou, Adam J. Spiers
papers.evidence: 低成本柔性触觉阵列测量三轴力用于机器人手
papers.tldr: 柔性触觉阵列通常仅能测量法向力，难以感知对稳定抓取至关重要的剪切力。VecTile采用压阻层与被动硅胶凸块结合，将三维力转化为可区分的压力模式，实现低成本柔性三轴力传感。在法向一至五牛、剪切最高一点五牛测试中，法向与剪切力均方根误差分别为零点三九牛和零点一六牛。该传感器能阻止手术刀刺破气球，并显著提升机器人在扩散策略引导下的电源插头插入性能。
papers.abstract_en: Tactile sensing provides robots with contact information difficult to obtain from vision alone. Shear force is particularly important for understanding tangential contact, guiding corrective motions, and maintaining grasp stability, yet flexible and low-cost tactile arrays often measure only normal force. We introduce VecTile, a low-cost, 6 mm thin, flexible tactile array capable of three-axis force sensing. VecTile combines a piezoresistive layer with passive silicone nubs that convert normal and shear forces into distinguishable pressure patterns. The sensor can be fabricated in-house without specialized equipment. The complete system costs less than 35 USD for a 4x4 array. We validate the sensing mechanism through finite element analysis and hardware experiments. In controlled single-taxel tests over 1-5 N normal force and up to 1.5 N shear force, VecTile achieves root-mean-square errors of 0.39 N and 0.16 N for normal and shear forces. A VecTile calibrated while flat retains accuracy when curved, while a five-minute manual calibration is sufficient for practical use. Two applications demonstrate its utility. First, shear readings are sensitive enough to stop a sharp scalpel from puncturing a balloon after contact. Second, the sensor substantially improves Diffusion Policy-guided power-plug insertion. All designs and code will be released upon paper acceptance. Project website: https://jiannnh.github.io/VecTile/.

papers.title_en: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing
papers.authors: Ariel Slepyan, Geeta Chandra Raju Bethala, Jiafeng Gu, Anagha Rajendra Dangle, Yinzhe Zhou, Hongyuan Fu, Jade Sim, Tuhin Basu, Xinyi Yin, Md Faizal Karim, Gregory Hager, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Anand Bhattad, Krishna Murthy Jatavallabhula, Nitish V. Thakor
papers.evidence: OpenTac提供可定制的触觉皮肤，用于下游机器人控制与学习应用。
papers.tldr: 现有触觉皮肤定制困难、扩展性差且迁移受限，制约机器人灵巧操作。OpenTac采用结构化可变形覆盖层的电阻式皮肤，将切向载荷转为空间压力，差分响应解码剪切、共模响应编码法向力。其CAD工具可从2D轮廓、可展开3D表面甚至文本自动生成制造文件，并配套模拟器与跨传感器迁移。已制造30余种传感器并在四个机器人上验证，自适应采集千赫兹率比全阵列快19.2倍，为触觉感知提供开放生态。
papers.abstract_en: We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold. First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force. Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text (e.g., "design a sensor for a size 9 shoe insole"). We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments. We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments. Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, exceeding full-array raster scanning on the same sensor by 19.2X at 16 sampled taxels per update for a 1024-taxel skin. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos are at opentac.github.io

papers.title_en: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Xiao Tan, Yixuan Wang, Zhexi Wang, Wenzhen Yuan
papers.evidence: 用于接触丰富操作的力/力矩测量编码智能体
papers.tldr: 接触丰富机器人操作中，编程智能体需要响应物理交互。FORCA结合视觉观察与腕部力/扭矩，编写并迭代修正Python程序，实现力响应运动与接触探测。在五个真实机器人任务中，FORCA相比仅视觉变体显著提高抓取精度、任务成功率，并减少擦拭和剥离中的接触丢失。无需演示或训练，展示了力感知编程智能体在动态接触场景中的通用性与有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Coding agents can translate language instructions into robot programs. For contact-rich manipulation, a key challenge is to generate and refine control logic that responds to physical interaction. We present FORCA, a coding agent that takes visual observations and wrist force/torque (F/T) measurements as input to write Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion. Between executions, the agent inspects force records alongside visual outcomes to diagnose failures and revise both motion and force-feedback control logic. FORCA requires no demonstrations, task-specific training, or simulation. Across five real-robot tasks, we demonstrate its effectiveness in three forms of contact-rich manipulation: improving manipulation accuracy, adapting to changes in object or surface properties, and regulating contact under surface variation and object motion. Compared with a vision-only variant of the same agent, FORCA improves grasp accuracy and task success and reduces contact loss in wiping and peeling.

papers.title_en: DEX-PHD: A Dexterous Portable Handheld Device for Multimodal Data Collection
papers.authors: Jooyoung Hong, Noboru Myers, Obin Kwon, Yixian Yang, Joohyung Kim
papers.evidence: 灵巧手持设备记录指尖接触数据用于接触丰富操作
papers.tldr: 现有操作数据收集方法难以同时兼顾精确性和便携性，运动链遥操作精确但受限于固定环境，视觉方法便携但精度较低。DEX-PHD是一个便携手持设备，集成灵巧机器人手、逐指连续控制和多模态记录，能采集本体感觉、指尖接触和腕部相机视频，且无绳设计支持多样环境。在接触丰富的多指协调任务上演示并部署到物理人形机器人，开环重放保留了手指运动的主要时间模式和任务相关接触。该设备为便携式多模态灵巧操作数据收集提供了实用平台。
papers.abstract_en: Existing manipulation data collection methods typically offer either accurate robot-state acquisition through kinematic-chain-based teleoperation or convenient, portable operation through vision-based approaches. We present DEX-PHD, a portable handheld device that combines these advantages for dexterous manipulation by integrating a dexterous robot hand, continuous per-finger control, and multimodal logging. The system records proprioceptive information, fingertip contact data, and wrist-camera video, while the operator directly controls the robot hand through joint-level mapping. Its untethered design enables data collection across diverse environments. We demonstrate DEX-PHD on contact-rich tasks requiring coordinated multi-finger manipulation and deploy the collected demonstrations through open-loop replay on a physical humanoid robot. The results show that open-loop replay preserves the main temporal patterns of finger motion and task-relevant contact. Therefore, DEX-PHD provides a practical platform for portable, multimodal dexterous manipulation data collection.

papers.title_en: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Sihang Li, Xiaofeng Guo, Jinkun Cao, Charlie Cheng, Ruihan Yang, Chen Feng, Guanya Shi, Haozhi Qi
papers.evidence: 使用力传感夹爪和接触力矩学习力反应式人形操作
papers.tldr: 人形机器人操作需同时控制接触力和运动，且力需双手与全身协调，仅靠运动学轨迹难以表达。本文提出FLORE框架，利用力传感手持夹爪和可穿戴跟踪器采集无机器人示教，以力反应扩散策略从视觉、本体感觉和力旋量预测动作及双手力命令。混合柔顺全身控制器通过力误差积分实现精准力跟踪和平衡保持。仿真显示力跟踪对全身运动精度影响小，真实机器人三项接触任务成功率达80%，远超仅位置策略的26.7%，表明力控制对接触丰富操作至关重要。
papers.abstract_en: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.

papers.title_en: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.authors: Cunxi Dai, Botao He, Francois R Hogan, Wei Pan, Rao Fu, Wen-Han Hsieh, Ruoshi Liu, Jitendra Malik, Guanya Shi, Akash Sharma
papers.evidence: 接触锚定的重定向保留触觉手套的接触力目标用于灵巧操作
papers.tldr: 传统机器人数据收集限制人类灵巧性，现有重定向仅转换运动学、忽略接触动力学。提出CARD框架，通过共享手-接触表示统一视频、动捕和触觉手套数据，显式保留接触力目标，并引入触觉跟踪控制器；针对视频提出Vid-HACO模型。在多种数据源上CARD保持接触帧43-78%，远超现有方法，集成物理重定向使任务成功率从12%提升至32%。接触保留提供可扩展的灵巧性传递接口。
papers.abstract_en: Humans are dexterous, but traditional data collection paradigms such as teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and wearable exoskeletons force humans to act through the robot embodiment, bottlenecking their dexterity. Retargeting can avoid this. However, existing methods purely translate kinematics and ignore the real-world contact dynamics essential for task success. We present CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation, a simulator and object-free framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions by explicitly preserving contact force targets. CARD unifies human data sources including video, motion capture, and tactile gloves via a shared hand--contact representation and generates explicit contact force targets in addition to kinematics. To maintain these contact targets during hardware open-loop replay, CARD also introduces a tactile tracking controller. For video which does not contain an explicit tactile source, we present Vid-HACO, our video-to-contact model that sets a new state of the art. Across our video, glove, motion-capture data and the GRAB dataset, CARD maintains contact on $43$--$78\%$ of contact frames, while kinematic and object-aware retargeting methods maintain contact on $<10\%$ and $22.5\%$ of the frames respectively. Further, integrating our formulation into physics-based retargeting improves strict task success from 12\% to 32\% on GRAB dataset. Finally, we show that our tactile tracker is critical to reproduce demonstrated forces during hardware replay. These results establish that contact preservation via CARD is a scalable interface for transferring human dexterity to robots.

papers.title_en: ActiveAlign: Aligning Egocentric Manipulation via Active Perception
papers.authors: Ri-Zhao Qiu, Bowen Wen, Yifeng Jiang, Chen Tessler, Eric Heiden, Xue Bin Peng, Xiaolong Wang, Stan Birchfield, Erwin Coumans
papers.evidence: ActiveAlign-Touching通过触觉反馈细化物体对齐
papers.tldr: 现有Real2Sim2Real方法多依赖被动感知，导致现实与仿真间存在观测差距。ActiveAlign框架通过主动感知对齐这一差距，包含ActiveAlign-Waving利用主动手部运动与可微渲染进行手眼标定，以及ActiveAlign-Touching借助触觉反馈精调物体位姿至毫米级。在真实Unitree G1机器人上实现了按按钮、移动滑块等毫米级精细操作，并可用于无标定机器人数据集的仿真环境构建，显著提升真实到仿真的对齐能力。
papers.abstract_en: Real-to-Sim-to-Real (Real2Sim2Real) enables structured world representations for planning, interpretability, and safe execution. Most existing approaches rely on passive perception, which creates real2sim gaps due to imperfect observation. Inspired by how humans perceive actively through actions, we propose ActiveAlign, a framework that leverages active perception to align the Real2Sim2Real gap from interactions. ActiveAlign introduces two complementary modules: (i) ActiveAlign-Waving, which performs hand-eye calibration by exploiting active hand motions and differentiable rendering, and (ii) ActiveAlign-Touching, which refines object alignment through tactile feedback to achieve millimeter-level precision. Together, these capabilities enable strong real2sim alignment. We demonstrate that ActiveAlign-Waving can be used to curate simulation environments for open-sourced uncalibrated robot manipulation datasets, and demonstrate on a real Unitree G1 robot that ActiveAlign enables fine manipulation of millimeter-scale objects such as pressing buttons and moving sliders.

papers.title_en: Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills via Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking
papers.authors: Yuxuan Kuang, Jiashun Wang, Yixuan Sun, Yufei Ye, Sungjae Park, Umar Iqbal, Katerina Fragkiadaki, Shubham Tulsiani
papers.evidence: 混合灵巧模仿从单一轨迹学习可适应的灵巧技能，无触觉
papers.tldr: 现有灵巧手技能学习存在泛化与人类先验的权衡：目标强化学习泛化但策略不自然，运动跟踪复制人类却无法偏离。AdaDex框架将几秒人类手-物轨迹转为可适应灵巧技能，核心是混合灵巧模仿，在运动跟踪和泛化环境两个群体上训练共享策略。结果可学习功能性抓取、物体移位、手指步态手中重定向及抛接等多样技能，并优于基线。该方法实现了从少量人类示范学习可泛化灵巧技能，具备跨模拟器和真实世界迁移能力。
papers.abstract_en: Dexterous multi-finger hands hold promise to unlock diverse skills like functional grasps, in-hand reorientation, and dynamic handover that the human-designed world assumes, yet existing learning recipes force a trade-off. Goal-reaching reinforcement learning generalizes to arbitrary object poses but, lacking any human prior, converges to unnatural and unreliable finger strategies; motion tracking reproduces human-like behavior from a single clip but cannot deviate from it. We present AdaDex, a goal-conditioned RL framework that turns a single hand-object trajectory of a few seconds---from mocap data or HOI reconstruction from in-the-wild RGB(D) video---into an adaptable dexterous skill. At the core of AdaDex is Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking: a shared policy is trained on two populations of massively parallel environments: motion tracking environments trained with dense motion tracking objective, which instill the human prior from human motion; and generalization environments with noised initial states and goals and a sparse object-success reward, which force the skill to work far off the reference. From seconds of human motion per skill, the resulting policies can learn diverse adaptable dexterous skills, such as functional grasping, object reposing, in-hand reorientation with finger gaiting, and dynamic behaviors like throw-and-catch. Our method outperforms baselines in terms of generalization and functionality, and we demonstrate transfer across simulators and to the real world. Project page: https://yuxuank.com/AdaDex/.

papers.title_en: Training in Deployment: Human-in-the-loop Online Post-Training for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Chun Gu, Xiaofei Wei, Yiming Chen, Bozhou Zhang, Juntong Zhang, Xiatian Zhu, Li Zhang
papers.evidence: 人在环路的在线后训练用于接触丰富的机器人操作
papers.tldr: 大型预训练机器人基础模型在适应目标任务时，离线遥操作演示难以覆盖部署中接触丰富、恢复和精度关键状态；离线后训练适应慢，在线强化学习则复杂且不稳定。为此，提出TIDE系统，采用provenance-conditioned监督学习，从人类干预和策略生成rollouts在线更新策略，无需critic或奖励模型。在四个真实双臂操作任务上，TIDE显著提升任务进度和完成率，且与固定策略基线相当，每任务训练不足一小时。该框架实现了部署中高效稳定的人类在环在线后训练，为机器人操作适应提供新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Large pretrained robot foundation models provide strong priors for manipulation, yet adapting them to target tasks with offline teleoperated demonstrations often fails to cover the contact-rich, recovery, and precision-critical states encountered during deployment. Existing methods mitigate this issue by augmenting offline demonstrations with human-in-the-loop data or online reinforcement learning. Despite this, offline post-training adapts slowly because it cannot immediately absorb deployment experience, while online RL typically relies on value functions or auxiliary actor-critic models, increasing both training complexity and instability. We present TIDE (Training In DEployment), a human-in-the-loop online post-training system. TIDE introduces a provenance-conditioned supervised learning framework that updates the policy online from human interventions and policy-generated rollouts collected during deployment, without a learned critic, reward model, or action scorer. Across four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, TIDE improves milestone-normalized task progress and binary full-task completion over the warm-start policy and matched additional offline demonstrations, and performs comparably to the fixed-policy collection baseline while making updated checkpoints available during deployment. Each task-specific online post-training session, from the start of deployment rollouts until the final checkpoint is available, completes in less than one hour while learning and checkpoint handling run asynchronously.

papers.title_en: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Likui Zhang, Zhe Zhu, Zhihao Zhan, Yibo Bai, Hanlin Wang, Dongwei Li, Bin Wang, Tianle Zhang, Xiaodan Liang, Liang Lin
papers.evidence: 用于长程机器人操作的强化学习后训练
papers.tldr: 现有视觉-语言-动作模型的强化学习后训练面临稀疏奖励下信用分配偏差与子任务瓶颈，制约长程操作。AtomicRL 引入原子任务结构，通过语义感知策略优化约束失败子任务的 TD 残差传播，并利用瓶颈自适应探索聚焦未掌握环节。在 LIBERO-LONG 和 CALVIN ABC-D 上分别提升最高 4.0% 和 9.5%，结合 Real2Sim2Real 真实任务平均提升 21.3%。该框架显著改善长程机器人操作的学习效率与性能。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration. AtomicRL introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses semantic-aware gating to constrain TD residuals from failed atomic subtasks from propagating across task boundaries, mitigating credit contamination while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping. In addition, Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration (BATE) dynamically coordinates task sampling and local exploration incentives based on the mastery of individual atomic subtasks, directing learning toward the remaining bottlenecks. Finally, we develop a Real2Sim2Real pipeline that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots. On LIBERO-LONG, AtomicRL achieves absolute performance gains of 3.6% and 4.0% over PPO across two VLA architectures. On CALVIN ABC-D, it improves full-task performance by up to 9.5% over PPO. Combined with the Real2Sim2Real pipeline, AtomicRL further improves real-world task performance by an average of 21.3%. These results demonstrate that AtomicRL effectively improves the learning efficiency and manipulation performance of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks.

papers.title_en: CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
papers.authors: Houzhu Ding, Xinda Qi, Luqi Wang, Ming Yang
papers.evidence: CW-WAM预测接触力用于力敏感操作，实现接触丰富控制。
papers.tldr: 力敏感操作需要接触与负载信息，而视觉观察无法直接提供。CW-WAM世界行动模型联合预测视频、运动和接触力矩，并作为导纳控制器的力参考。该模型将方形销钉插入成功率从25%提升至70%，电源适配器从40%提升至95%，同时显著降低力参考误差。此框架为力敏感操作提供了有效的控制参考和预测能力。
papers.abstract_en: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predicted wrench chunk acts as a force reference for a 20-Hz outer-loop admittance controller within a slow-fast control system that maintains force feedback and smooth motion between model queries. CW-WAM improves contact prediction and increases the insertion success rate from 25% to 70% for square pegs with 1-mm clearance per side and from 40% to 95% for power adapters, compared with WAM without wrench input. It also improves lifting-height accuracy across different loads. Our framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE from 4.8 to 2.7 N for peg insertion and from 2.0 to 1.3 N for wiping, respectively, with smaller force fluctuations during successful execution. Project website: https://cw-wam-project.github.io/

papers.title_en: Reconstruction-Augmented Visuomotor Pre-Training of 3D-Grounded Bimanual Dexterity from RGB-Only Human Videos
papers.authors: Xingyi He, Zhiwen Qiu, Adhitya Polavaram, Yunhao Cao, Cory Fan, Julius Samwer, Saleh Kalantari, Kuan Fang
papers.evidence: 通过重构增强的视觉运动预训练从RGB人体视频学习双手灵巧操作
papers.tldr: 从RGB-only人类视频学习双手灵巧操作面临挑战，因为缺乏3D空间上下文，难以将行为与场景几何对齐。SpatialDex通过从每个视频重建场景几何并估计手部运动，利用手部尺寸先验对齐，将几何同时作为策略输入和预测目标。在1M人类视频片段上预训练后，该方法在9个模拟灵巧任务和6个真实世界双手任务上分别超越现有方法16.5和38.3点。研究表明重建增强预训练能够有效注入3D grounding，显著提升双手灵巧操作性能。
papers.abstract_en: We present SpatialDex, a framework that learns 3D-grounded bimanual dexterity from RGB-only human videos through reconstruction-augmented visuomotor pre-training. The central idea is to learn human behavior together with its spatial context. From each video, we reconstruct the scene geometry and estimate the hand motion, align them at a shared video-level scale using the hand-size prior of 3D hand estimates. We retain the reconstructed geometry as both a policy input and a prediction target. The policy grounds the token grid of a pre-trained vision-language model in this geometry through gated residual fusion, is trained to predict future scene geometry alongside wrist and finger actions, and generates finger motion conditioned on the predicted trajectories of both wrists. Pre-trained on 1M human-video clips and fine-tuned with a small number of robot demonstrations, SpatialDex outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by 16.5 points on nine simulated dexterous tasks across two embodiments and by 38.3 points on six real-world bimanual dexterous tasks. Under a matched comparison, pre-training with reconstructed geometry improves success by 14.2 points over pre-training on hand motion alone.

papers.title_en: DeXplicit: Making Physical State Explicit in Dexterous Manipulation World Models
papers.authors: Adam Lee, Mutian Xu, Yukang Cao, Shulin Tian, Ziwei Liu
papers.evidence: 灵巧操作世界模型预测显式三维物理状态用于技能学习
papers.tldr: 现有灵巧操作模型常将动力学与视觉合成纠缠，缺乏对象结构。DeXplicit 先显式预测度量3D对象运动与变形，再渲染视觉结果，提供结构化未来状态作为视频生成强先验，使渲染器专注新可见内容。在三个基准上，该方法将移动点误差降低 27-40%，HOT3D 对象保真 IoU+ 提升 47%，两步骤因果生成提速 57 倍，实现高效几何一致的世界建模。
papers.abstract_en: Before acting on an object, a robot needs to anticipate how its hand motion will change the physical world and what the resulting scene will look like. Existing approaches typically entangle action-conditioned dynamics, camera motion, and visual synthesis within a video generation model, or represent dynamics as point trajectories without explicit object structure. We introduce DeXplicit, a dexterous manipulation world model that instead predicts how the world evolves explicitly in metric 3D before rendering its visual consequences. Given an initial scene and a future hand trajectory, a lightweight 3D dynamics network predicts object-centric motion and deformation, providing structured and geometrically grounded future world states. These predictions then serve as a strong scaffold for video generation: appearance is transported through the predicted 3D motion and projected into future views, allowing the renderer to focus on completing uncertain and newly visible content rather than implicitly learning world dynamics from pixels. This explicit-3D-first decomposition also enables efficient causal generation, requiring only two denoising steps per block while conditioning on generated history.   Across HOT3D, OakInk2, and PhysTwin, DeXplicit reduces moved-point error by 27-40% relative to PointWorld and improves object fidelity IoU+ by 47% on HOT3D under a shared renderer. Our design with two-step causal generation achieves a 57x speedup from our 14B bi-directional configuration in video synthesis.

papers.title_en: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
papers.authors: Amber Xie, Jiawei Fu, Xiaofeng Guo, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi, Haozhi Qi
papers.evidence: 用于高自由度灵巧手的便携式数据采集接口
papers.tldr: 高质量演示是学习灵巧操作的主要瓶颈，遥控操作需要完整机器人设置且操作者协调手指负担重，人类演示还需运动估计与重定向。DexPort 作为便携式数据收集接口，使用与部署相同的手硬件，操作者通过手腕运动指定机器人末端位姿，并选择或调整技能来协调手指运动，无需独立控制每个关节。在实验室和野外采集超过2500个演示，用行为克隆直接训练视觉运动策略，无需技能标签。结果显示使用记录的机器人命令而非状态将成功率从11%提升到64%，使用野外数据后任务成功率从36%提升到78%。
papers.abstract_en: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.

papers.title_en: Learning Dexterous Manipulation: Hands, Simulators, Training, and Evaluation
papers.authors: Luai Abuelsamen
papers.evidence: 基于学习的灵巧操作方法的综述
papers.tldr: 灵巧操作领域近年快速发展，论文数量自2022年增长三倍。该综述系统梳理113种学习方法，发现主流方案为在GPU模拟器中使用特权状态强化学习，再蒸馏为纯视觉策略迁移硬件；另一快速分支则基于遥操作演示与扩散策略。抓取仍为最大任务家族，双手协调增长最快，实验集中于四款主流灵巧手。作者结合代码与供应商规格核对，揭示深度测量等关键报告缺失，并提出统一评测协议。
papers.abstract_en: A dexterous hand can change an object's pose without setting it down. This survey covers 113 learning-based methods that attempt it, the hands they run on, the simulators they train in, and how they report results. The field has largely converged on one recipe: reinforcement learning on privileged state in a GPU simulator, distilled into a vision-only student for transfer to hardware. Almost half the corpus trains that way, nearly all of it in one simulator, whose own successors are barely used. A second and faster-growing branch learns from teleoperated demonstration instead, through vision-language-action models, diffusion policies, and systems whose contribution is the collection rig itself. Published work has tripled since 2022. Grasping remains the largest task family and bimanual coordination the fastest-rising, and almost every experiment runs on one of four hands. What the survey adds comes from reading released code and vendor specifications beside the papers. Eight hands that can be bought or built from published designs appear in no method paper here. Where the depth a hand sinks into the object it holds is reported at all, it is not measured in the physics that produced the motion. Section VII proposes a protocol for the unreported quantities; the body gives the counts behind every claim above.

papers.title_en: AWLS: Advantage-Weighted Latent Steering for One-Step Generative Robotic Manipulation Policies
papers.authors: Jiahong Tang, Jiaju He, Zhiyuan Yang, Ruyang Han, Haiyue Zhu
papers.evidence: 利用优势加权潜在转向改进机器人操作策略
papers.tldr: 真实机器人操作演示常包含混合质量轨迹，标准行为克隆均等拟合所有动作，易重现次优模式。AWLS提出优势加权潜在引导方法，在冻结的一步生成策略上学习观测条件残差噪声塑形器，并以优势加权动作重构目标训练。实验在模拟与真实机器人操作任务上显示，AWLS相比冻结基策略性能提升，同时限制偏离预训练行为先验。该方法避免更新解码器与critic梯度，保持单步推理，并引入无rollout的解码器敏感性准则选择可引导检查点。
papers.abstract_en: Human-collected real-world robotic manipulation demonstrations often contain mixed-quality trajectories, including hesitant, indirect, or inefficient action segments. While diffusion- and flow-based policies can model such multimodal data, standard behavior cloning (BC) assigns equal likelihood to all demonstrated actions and may therefore reproduce suboptimal modes. Offline RL value estimates offer a natural signal for biasing policies toward higher-value behavioral modes, but directly fine-tuning the generative policy or using critic gradients for policy steering can amplify critic errors and induce prior drift. We propose Advantage-Weighted Latent Steering (AWLS), an offline post-training method for improving frozen one-step generative manipulation policies without updating their decoders. AWLS learns a residual noise shaper, an observation-conditioned residual correction to the policy's latent noise, and trains it with an advantage-weighted action reconstruction objective. The advantages are detached, scale-normalized, and used only as supervised weights on demonstrated actions, avoiding critic-gradient policy updates while preserving fast single-step inference. We further introduce a rollout-free decoder-sensitivity criterion for selecting pretrained checkpoints that remain responsive to latent-noise perturbations. Experiments on simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks with clean and mixed-quality demonstrations show that AWLS improves over the frozen base policy while limiting drift from the pretrained behavior prior. Project page: https://awls-corl2026.github.io/

papers.title_en: Mixture of Flow Matching and Particle Filter for Proprioception-Based Online Contact Estimation
papers.authors: Seo Wook Han, Min Jun Kim
papers.evidence: 基于本体的在线接触估计确定接触位置和力用于接触丰富操作
papers.tldr: 本体感觉接触估计是机器人操作中的关键难题。针对仅依赖关节扭矩与基座力/扭矩传感器的病态逆问题，ContactFlowFilter创新融合流匹配模型与粒子滤波：递归结构刻画时序依赖，流匹配作为辅助提议分布捕捉多模态并检测接触事件。仿真与真实实验表明，单/双接触定位误差分别低至0.36 cm和0.88 cm，耗时仅0.69 ms和2.69 ms。该方法显著提升了接触估计精度与实时性。
papers.abstract_en: In this article, we propose ContactFlowFilter, a novel approach for contact estimation that determines the number of active contacts, their locations, and the associated force vectors. We consider a robot manipulator equipped with joint torque sensors and a base force/torque sensor; such a proprioceptive-only setup presents a challenging inverse problem characterized by (i) multi-modality from non-unique solutions, (ii) temporal dependencies in state evolution, and (iii) discrete contact events involving contact addition/removal. Existing approaches, such as particle filters (PFs) and learning-based methods, often struggle to address these challenges simultaneously. To overcome this, ContactFlowFilter integrates a generative model into the PF framework. The recursive structure of the PF captures temporal dependencies, while the flow matching model serves as an auxiliary proposal distribution to track multi-modal beliefs and detect contact events. Extensive validation in both simulation and real-world experiments confirms the effectiveness of the proposed method. In real-world settings, ContactFlowFilter achieves the lowest dissimilarity from the target distribution, with errors of only 0.36 cm and 0.88 cm for single- and dual-contact scenarios, respectively, while operating at 0.69 ms and 2.69 ms.

papers.title_en: TEAR: Task-Evidence Authority Routing for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Shicheng Zhang, Hui Liu, Haoliang Li
papers.evidence: 面向接触丰富机器人操作的控制权限路由
papers.tldr: 野外机器人操作需动态分配人类遥操作与本地自主的控制权限，二者可靠性互补。TEAR框架在机器人侧利用网络状态证据和任务语义证据，通过轻量时序仲裁器结合机器人状态与当前权限定时切换。在模拟和真实动态网络试验中，TEAR任务成功率接近纯遥操作，但仅需19.8%-27.4%的遥操作控制步，较纯自主提升30-40%成功率。该互补控制权路由方案显著减少了对持续人工控制的依赖，同时维持高成功率。
papers.abstract_en: Reliable robotic manipulation in field-deployed settings requires more than executing a capable controller. As the execution conditions change, the system must decide, online and on the robot side, which control source should hold authority. Human teleoperation adapts readily to contact-rich and semantically ambiguous situations but depends on a stable communication link. Local autonomy is executed without continuous human intervention, but may fail under semantic ambiguity, long-horizon drift, and unforeseen contingencies. These two control sources exhibit complementary reliability profiles. We formulate this complementarity as a control authority routing problem and present Task-Evidence Authority Routing for Robotic Manipulation (TEAR), an edge-deployable framework that allocates authority between human teleoperation and local autonomy. TEAR arbitrates on the robot side using network-state evidence, which governs the usability of teleoperation, and task-semantic evidence, which reflects whether autonomous execution remains consistent with the current task. A lightweight temporal arbitrator observes both forms of evidence together with robot state and current authority to time authority transfers. Across simulated and real-world trials under dynamic network conditions, TEAR achieves task success rates close to pure teleoperation while limiting teleoperation to 19.8-27.4% of control steps and improves success by 30-40% over autonomy-only execution in our settings. These results demonstrate the potential of complementary authority routing to sustain successful manipulation with substantially reduced dependence on continuous human control.
